title: MSK: managed Kafka still needs event design
outcome: Map broker management, clients, network, identity, partitions, and consumer operations in AWS.
useCase: The local Rails/Kafka design moved to a managed AWS environment.
drawbacks: Client integration, business correctness, and recovery remain yours.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Managed brokers, still your event contract.

trace.title: Client network and identity
trace.detail: MSK provides managed Kafka options. It reduces parts of broker infrastructure work, but does not choose event keys, schemas, consumer groups, offset policy, or business idempotence for you. Provisioned/serverless options have different configuration and capacity contracts.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Client contacts bootstrap → discovers leaders → authenticates/connects to actual brokers → produces keyed record → group consumes/commits under its own policy. Debug network, auth, topic access, and business processing separately.

Retention and consumer downtime interact. A lagging consumer can lose required history after retention; managed brokers do not extend the business recovery window automatically.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: MSK does not make a Rails DB write and Kafka publish atomic. Client libraries can require explicit support for the selected authentication method. A topic with one hot key can bottleneck despite more brokers.
